newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak PM Meciar sees GDP up 5-6 pct in '97, '98.
newsitem.headline: Slovak PM Meciar sees GDP up 5-6 pct in '97, '98.

text.p: Slovakia's gross domestic product (GDP) should grow by between five and six percent in 1997 and 1998, Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said in a televised discussion programme on Thursday.
"The tendency is that GDP should grow by around five to six percent this year and next year," Meciar said.
GDP was up 5.1 percent year-on-year in real terms in the first quarter of this year, down from 7.3 percent real GDP growth for the same period in 1996. GDP rose 6.9 percent in 1996.
"The slowdown in GDP growth should end at around the latest published levels," Meciar said.
But he added that he was not satisfied with the predicted growth rate.
"The question is whether this prediction is (considered) a fast or slow increase....I say it's slow," Meciar said.
He did not elaborate as to precisely what level of GDP growth rate the government would be satisfied with.
The Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) has forecast GDP growth for the first half of this year at between 5.7 and 6.3 percent, expecting it to slow down to 5.6 percent for the full year.
The 1997 state budget is based on the assumption of GDP growth of at least six percent.
The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) has said it would welcome slower GDP growth this year.
